Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 31-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025/JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: ECE 1003/ECE_1003 FUNDAMENTALS OF ELECTRONICS  
  Fundamentals of Electronics [ECE 1003]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Consider a circuit shown in figure with V IN = 10 Sin(wt) and ideal diodes D1, D2 and D3.             (4)  
  (i) Sketch the waveform across the load resistance 'RL '.  
  (ii) Determine the DC and RMS value of load currents for a load resistance of RL = 1KΩ.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               A Germanium diode carries a current of 10mA under a forward bias voltage of 0.3V at 27 o C. If the    (3)  
  reverse saturation current is 4.38µA, find the dynamic forward resistance at 40o C.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               Determine the range of input volage to obtain an output voltage of 6.3V in a Zener voltage regulator (3)  
  circuit. The current flowing through Zener diode ranges from 2mA to 28mA and the load resistance  
  is 1KΩ. Assume Rs = 470Ω. Draw the circuit diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               With a neat sketch, explain the pinch-off phenomenon in n-channel MOSFET. Calculate the bias        (4)  
  current of M1 shown in figure and determine its region of operation. Assume µn C ox = 100 µA/V2 and  
  $$VTH = 0.5V.$$  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)   For a self-bias MOSFET circuit, determine the bias current of MOSFET assuming VTH = 0.4V,               (3)  
  µ n C ox = 100µA/V2 , W/L = 4/0.18, R1 =5KΩ, R2 =12KΩ, Rs=1KΩ and VDD=1.8V. Also, find the  
  maximum value of drain resistance RD, for MOSFET to remain in saturation. Assume  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2C)   Explain the working of a square wave generator using OP-AMP.                                            (3)  
  In this circuit if all the resistors are 10KΩ, C= 0.1µF and ±Vsat =12V, determine the frequency of  
  oscillation of the output square wave signal  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)   i) With relevant circuit diagram and equations, explain the working of an OPAMP integrator.             (4)  
  ii) Given three input voltage sources V1 =1V, V2 = sin (wt) and V3 = cos (wt) , design a two stage  
  OPAMP circuit to obtain V 0 = 10 + 5Sin(wt) - 5cos(wt). Assume feedback resistor to be usedRF =  
  10KΩ.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)   (i) Convert (0101)2 into Gray Code.                                                                     (3)  
  
  (ii) Perform (45.75)10 - (87.75)10 subtraction using 1's complement method.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3C)   (i) Encrypt the data 1001 using (7,4) even parity bit Hamming code.                                     (3)  
  (ii) Consider a new message encrypted as "1110110" using (7,4) even parity bit Hamming code  
  transmitted through a noisy channel. Decode the message, assuming that there can be maximum  
  of one bit error in the encrypted message received.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)   Solve F=Σ(1,5,6,12,13,14)+d(2,4) using K-Map and implement resultant expression using only              (4)  
  NAND gates.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4B)   A logic system has 3 inputs and one output, the output of the system is low only when any two of   (3)  
  the inputs are high. Write the truth table and standard SOP. Also implement the system using basic  
  gates.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4C)   Draw the logic diagram of a 3-bit ripple down-counter using the positive edge-triggered T flip flops.   (3)  
  Plot the timing diagram for the same.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  Page #2

5A)                   Design a 4-bit Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO) shift register using D flip-flops.                         (4)  
  (a) Draw the logic diagram showing how the flip-flops are connected.  
  (b) If the input data sequence is 1101, show the contents of each flip-flop (Q₃ Q₂ Q₁ Q₀) after every  
  clock pulse.  
  (c) How many clock pulses are required for the entire data to appear at the output of the register?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)                   Compare the operation of SR, JK, D, and T flip-flops in terms of input conditions, and invalid states. (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5"  
  
$$5C)                   Simplify and implement F(A, B,C)=A′ B′ C+ A B′ C′ + A B′ C using an 4:1 MUX.                           (3)$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5"
